newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--The confusion over the completion of the E9 real estate declaration form has forced Deputy Finance Minister George Drys to extend the submission dates for all tax declarations.

--As conservative opposition ND deputy Kostas Karamanlis keeps his cards close to his chest on whether he has accepted the proposal to run for the party's leadership, incumbent Miltiades Evert yesterday defiantly said he would stand for the post. His main challenger George Souflias, meanwhile, told an enthusiastic crowd of supporters last night that he was confident of victory.

--A serious obstacle to today's scheduled EU-Cyprus Association Council meeting arose at yesterday's meeting of the Council of Ministers. Germany, Britain and France are now pressuring Athens to accept to the participation of Turkish Cypriots in the accession process.
--Impressive archaeological finds from the Early Christian period have come to light at digs in Santorini.

--Striking teachers have decided to continue their labour action for a seventh week while Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis calls on them to come forward with specific proposals on their institutional demands.

--Teachers will join today's 24-hour strike and rally by civil servants. Meanwhile, municipality workers yesterday decided on rolling 48-hour strikes after a fruitless meeting at the interior ministry. The strike will affect garbage collection in the wider Athens area.

--Efforts to block Cyprus's accession to the European Union will be met by a block on the EU's expansion eastwards and a veto on Turkey's relations with Europe, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos warned yesterday.

--A worker at a construction site in downtown Athens managed to smuggle priceless artefacts from an ancient grave to his home with the intention of selling them on the black market, police revealed yesterday.
--Britain's Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind is unequivocal: Britain does not want Cyprus in the EU before a solution is found.
--Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Onur Oymen says there are no borders in the Aegean and that they must be re-drawn.
--CNN is reported to be interested in an on-air replay of the phenomenally-successful Greek match-making show "Chrysso Koufeto".
--Euphoria on the Athens Stock Exchange as prices touch seven-year highs and turnover totals a record 34 billion drachmas.
--There's chaos at local tax offices as taxpayers and officials muddle through the maze of the E9 real estate declaration. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
